info.name: LogTrace API
info.description:
LogTrace© — AI-powered log intelligence for microservice environments.

**Auth:** All requests require `X-API-Key` header. Set the `api_key` variable in the active environment.

**Quick start:**
1. Import `LogTrace.postman_environment.json` and set it as active.
2. Set `api_key` to your key.
3. Run the **End-to-End Demo Flow** folder in sequence — submission IDs and incident IDs chain automatically via post-response scripts.

request.description:
Called by microservices or log shippers (Fluent Bit, Vector) on every log event. Writes directly to the per-service Redis Stream — no DB write in the hot path. The Stream Processor watches the stream and auto-triggers an incident when an anomaly pattern is detected.

**Rate limit:** 5,000 events/second across all services combined.

request.description:
Ask Nemotron Ultra 253B a follow-up question about the incident. The full incident context (all events, classifications, prior Q&A turns) is included in the prompt. Response is streamed as SSE tokens.

**Incident must be `complete`** before this endpoint is usable.

Example questions:
- `"Which other services might be affected that are not in these logs?"`
- `"Explain the cascade step by step as if I've never seen this codebase."`
- `"What monitoring alert would have caught this earlier?"`

**Note:** Postman buffers the full SSE response. For live token streaming use `curl -N` or the Investigation Portal.

item.name: End-to-End Demo Flow
item.description:
Run this folder as a **Collection Run** (Runner) to exercise the complete happy path in one click.

Each request auto-chains to the next via post-response variable saves:
1. Submit files → saves `submission_id`
2. Poll status → waits for `complete`
3. List incidents → saves `incident_id`
4. Get report → validates full schema
5. Chat → sends a follow-up question
6. Export → downloads Markdown

**Pre-requisite:** Upload two demo log files from `demo/payment-service.log` and `demo/order-service.log` (in the repository).

item.name: Demo Control
item.description:
Control the live cascade demo. These endpoints drive the `demo/producers/` services — start background traffic, trigger a cascade, check current demo phase, and reset state. Protected by the same `X-API-Key` header as all other endpoints.

**Typical demo sequence:**
1. `POST /demo/start` — producers begin normal background traffic
2. Wait 30–60s — let judges see normal operation
3. `POST /demo/cascade` — inject the payment-service cascade
4. `GET /demo/status` — confirm cascade is running
5. Watch the portal — Stream Processor auto-triggers within 60s
6. `POST /demo/reset` — clean up between demo runs

request.description:
Instructs all producer containers to begin pushing normal background traffic (INFO/DEBUG/occasional WARN) for `normal_duration_seconds`. Use this to establish baseline activity before triggering the cascade.

The API publishes a `demo:command:start` message to the Redis pub/sub channel that all producer containers subscribe to.

**Response:** Returns immediately with the demo session ID. Producers begin pushing within 1 second.

response.name: 200 Started

request.description:
Injects the cascade failure scenario immediately, regardless of whether normal traffic is running.

**What happens:**
1. A shared `trace_id` (UUID4) is generated and published to all producers
2. `payment-service` producer starts pushing `PoolTimeoutError` at ~1 error/2s
3. `order-service` producer starts pushing `UpstreamTimeoutError` after 1.2s delay
4. `api-gateway` producer starts pushing 503 errors after 2.8s delay
5. Stream Processor detects ERROR spike and auto-triggers within 60s

The `trace_id` is shared across all three services so trace-ID correlation fires.

**No manual action required after this call** — the system detects and analyses the cascade autonomously.

response.name: 200 Cascade Initiated
409 Cascade Already Running
response.body: { "detail": "A cascade is already in progress. Call POST /demo/reset first.", "phase": "cascade" }

request.description: Returns the current state of the demo session: which phase is active, how many events have been pushed per service, whether the Stream Processor has triggered, and the current submission/incident IDs if analysis has started.

exec: console.log('Demo phase:', body.phase, '| Events pushed:', JSON.stringify(body.events_pushed));

response.name: 200 Cascade Triggered
200 Idle

request.description:
Stops all producer activity, resets demo phase to `idle`, and optionally clears Redis Streams and/or DB submissions created during the demo run.

- `clear_redis_streams: true` — flushes all `stream:ingest:*` keys so the Stream Processor starts with a clean window (recommended between demo runs)
- `clear_db_submissions: false` — keeps past submissions and incidents in the DB so judges can browse previous runs in the portal

**Use between demo runs** to prevent the Stream Processor debounce from blocking a re-trigger.

exec: console.log('Demo reset. Ready for next run.');

response.name: 200 Reset

item.name: Connectors
item.description:
Manage log source connectors. Each connector pulls or receives events from an external ecosystem (AWS CloudWatch, Kafka, Sentry, etc.) and normalises them into LogTrace's event schema. All connectors feed the same Redis Streams pipeline — the analysis pipeline never knows the source.

**Supported connector types:** `http_push`, `otlp`, `cloudwatch`, `gcp_logging`, `azure_monitor`, `kafka`, `kinesis`, `pubsub`, `datadog_webhook`, `sentry_webhook`, `pagerduty_webhook`, `github_actions`, `elasticsearch_pull`, `file_watch`, `s3_bucket`

request.description: Returns all registered connectors with their current status. Credentials are never returned.

Register a new AWS CloudWatch Logs connector. LogTrace will poll the specified log group every 15 seconds, normalise each log event, and write it to the `payment-service` Redis Stream.

Credentials are encrypted at rest using AES-256 and are never returned by any GET endpoint.
